title: synthetic-dialogue-benchmark-with-incremental-kv-checkpointing
author: Priya Raman
release_notes: Add a new synthetic dialogue benchmark runner that produces incremental KV checkpoint artifacts and compact delta exports. Useful for KV-cache warmup experiments and mid-dialogue resume scenarios.
description:
Motivation: We need a repeatable, lightweight benchmark that approximates multi-turn chatbot traffic with realistic turn-length distributions and persona mixing while exercising the KV cache warmup/continuation paths. Current sequence replayers focus on single-turn mixes or long-seq workloads and do not support checkpointing/resume at arbitrary dialogue turns. This PR adds a synthetic-dialogue workload runner plus a small exporter that produces compact incremental KV checkpoint snapshots and per-turn delta telemetry to enable faster warm restarts and more precise warmup cost accounting.

What this PR does (single-string description): Adds a dialogue workload generator (dialog_replayer) that synthesizes conversations with configurable persona counts, turn-length distributions (empirical heavy-tail option), and controlled interleaving to create multi-user multiplexed chat traces. The runner supports two modes: "streaming-primer" that performs progressive KV priming (writes small incremental checkpoints after N turns) and "resume-verify" which replays from an exported checkpoint to measure continuation correctness and latency. A companion compact delta exporter writes gzipped line-delimited protobuf summaries (timestamp, turn_idx, token_counts, kv_changes_digest) which are intended for downstream aggregators without transferring full model state.

Design notes and constraints: Checkpoints are intentionally small: we only serialize the minimal KV changes required to reconstruct attention/kvcache for resumed generation (metadata + slices). The serialization format is versioned (v1) and documented in docs/bench_dialog.md. The runner is deterministic given a seed and includes a fast-mode that skips heavy-sampling to run thousands of short-dialogue traces for statistical power. The implementation avoids model-level dependencies by mocking tokenization boundaries for synthetic sequences; integration tests exercise end-to-end flow against a local lightweight inference shim that supports kvcache load/restore APIs.

Commit summary: 1) initial dialog replayer and API surface 2) incremental checkpoint serializer + compact delta exporter 3) reporter that aggregates per-turn latency, kv-hit-evolution, token-efficiency and writes a consolidated CSV for downstream analysis 4) integration test harness and smoke test that verifies resume fidelity 5) docs and example configs.

Files changed (high-level list included below) and small diffs: Add python runner at bench/runners/dialog_replayer.py, add exporter at bench/exporters/compact_delta_exporter.go, add reporter bench/reporters/dialog_aggregator.py, add integration test tests/integration/test_dialog_resume.py, add docs/docs/bench_dialog.md. Small tweaks to bench/common/checkpoint.go to expose a minimal serialize/deserialize interface.

How this helps: Enables controlled experiments on KV warmup strategies (frequency and granularity of incremental checkpoints) and measures the tradeoffs between warmup time and checkpoint size. It also allows platform teams to validate resume behavior for Private/Dedicated deployments and provides a compact telemetry artifact that can be uploaded to S3 or attached to perf dashboards without large storage costs.

Usage example (short): `python -m bench.runners.dialog_replayer --seed 42 --personas 50 --turns-per-dialog 6 --checkpoint-interval 3 --export-path out/` The exporter produces `out/checkpoints/*.v1.gz` and `out/aggregates/dialog_metrics.csv`.

Backward compatibility and risk: This only adds optional bench tooling and a new exporter. The only change touching runtime code is a small, well-reviewed interface in bench/common/checkpoint.go (non-breaking, adds an exported function). No production serving paths are modified.

Checklist: [x] design + docs updated, [x] unit & integration tests, [x] perf smoke ran locally, [x] reviewers added

Related work: builds on prior warmup experiments (see ENG-3498) and complements the session-replay runner by focusing on multi-turn resume fidelity and compact telemetry.

review_conversation: Diego Morales (2026-03-01): Nice direction — can you explain why you chose gzipped line-delimited protobuf instead of a small binary tarball?

Priya Raman (2026-03-01 reply): gzipped LD-Proto keeps streaming-friendly and lets downstream processors start aggregating before the full artifact is available. tarball would require full materialization and is heavier for S3+lambda workflows.

motivation: Provide a targeted benchmark to measure KV warmup/resume tradeoffs for multi-turn dialogue workloads and to produce compact telemetry artifacts for efficient storage/analysis.
notes_for_ops: Exporter artifacts are intentionally compact; consumer must implement incremental decode. New artifacts follow v1 schema located in docs/bench_dialog.md. No runtime rollout required.
impact_statement: Low risk — bench-only additions. Enables experiments that were previously costly to store and analyze. Provides a replayable deterministic workload to reproduce mid-dialogue resume regressions.
manual_testing: Ran 5k short-dialogue traces locally with seed-locked runs; validated resume fidelity against the local inference shim and compared latency deltas between coldstart and resume flows.
